# An Old Idea and a New Tool

## An Idea Nobody Could Test

More than 2,000 years ago, **Acharya Kanada** in India said that if you keep dividing matter, you reach particles too small to divide. He called them **parmanus**, and his ideas are recorded in the Sanskrit text, the *Vaisesika Sutras*. In Greece, **Leucippus** and **Democritus** had a similar idea and called these particles *atomos*, which means "indivisible".

These were careful ideas, but they were imagined, not tested. The particles were far too small to see, so nobody could check them.

<!-- STEP id="measure" -->
## Measuring Changed Everything

For centuries, people judged a change by what they could see. Wood burns to a small heap of ash, so it seemed that most of the wood had been destroyed. Then in the 1700s, chemists such as **Antoine Lavoisier** began to weigh everything before a change and after it, including the gases.

<!-- STEP id="takeaway" -->
## A Number Anyone Can Check

Your eyes can mislead you, but a balance gives a number that anyone can check, anywhere. Wood looks as if it disappears, yet the ash and the gases together have all the mass that went in.

**Measuring turned an old idea into something that could be tested.**
